# The derived files in this tree, the paths they are, and the one command that regenerates each.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (21/11). A generated file is committed and regenerated by hand, so two branches that
# are each correct alone make a STALE file when they meet: land243 added lua/core/agent_control.lua and its
# refusal codes, land244 was green because its narrowed gate never ran the refusal row, and main was red
# from bfad4f8f for the next landings. No worker could have prevented that - the only place that sees two
# branches at once is the merge. So the merge regenerates: the landing's merge step (lua/core/land.lua,
# M.regenerate) and the preflight run scripts/regenerate.sh on the merged tree and put what it wrote in the
# merge commit. The OUTPUT PATH is part of the line because a merge of two branches that both regenerated
# the same file is a CONFLICT in that file, and the merge may only resolve what this file declares is
# generated (M.merge_conflict): any other conflict stays a stop, for a person.
#
# FORMAT, one generator per line:   <output>[,<output>...] = <command>
#   the outputs are repo-relative, comma separated, with no spaces; the command is run with bash from the
#   tree root and everything after the first " = " belongs to it.
#
# THE RULES FOR ADDING A LINE, because a wrong line writes a wrong file into every landing:
#   * the output is a PURE FUNCTION OF THE TREE: same tree, same bytes, no clock, no network, no node,
#     no model, no database. A generator that reads the wall clock or a sibling checkout must not be here;
#   * it is IDEMPOTENT: a second run with nothing changed writes nothing (that is how the merge knows
#     whether to amend the commit at all, and scripts/test-regenerate.sh proves it);
#   * it needs nothing but the tree and the interpreter the fast path already requires (lua5.4, bash);
#   * every declared output must EXIST after the run (the runner refuses a generator that lies about what
#     it writes), and the check row that reads it must be a NEVER-DROPPED row (scripts/lib/fast-rows.sh,
#     wa_fast_core_rows - scripts/test-fast-rows.sh enforces that pairing).
#
# NOT here, with the reason, so nobody adds them by guess:
#   * fixtures/prompt-golden/ and the balloon snapshots (scripts/gen-balloon-snapshots.lua,
#     scripts/gen-balloon-before.lua): a golden is an APPROVAL - a changed byte is a decision a person
#     makes, and regenerating it inside a merge would approve whatever the round happened to produce;
#   * scripts/sync-prompt-docs.sh --write: NOT a pure function of the tree. It runs the generator inside a
#     wa binary (WA_BIN, else PATH, else ~/.local/bin/wa, else this tree's release build), so the bytes it
#     writes depend on which binary is installed, not on this tree - in a merged worktree that is the
#     operator's older binary, which would write a document this round never produced. Its own check
#     (prompt-docs in lua/core/land.lua M.DEFAULT_CHECKS) runs on every landing and is not narrowable, so
#     a stale block already reds the round it belongs to.
#
# Comments and blank lines are ignored.
lua/core/refusal_codes.lua = lua5.4 scripts/gen-refusal-codes.lua --write
# The WIT packages a component vendors in its `wit/deps/`: one canonical file each, sliced by a named
# keep list or copied whole (scripts/gen-wit-deps.lua, and its fast row scripts/test-wit-deps.lua).
# It belongs here rather than in a hand copy because a trimmed copy is a copy with an owner: measured
# 22/11, ten `kernel.wit` files in seven different contents, and the only thing that kept them from
# disagreeing on a function was that nobody had edited one yet.
rust/components/wa-email/wit/deps/kernel.wit,rust/components/wa-whatsapp/wit/deps/kernel.wit,rust/components/svc-drain/wit/deps/kernel.wit,rust/components/model-gateway/wit/deps/kernel.wit,rust/components/svc-queue-echo/wit/deps/kernel.wit,rust/components/telemetry-sink/wit/deps/kernel.wit,wit/memory/deps/kernel/kernel.wit,wit/selfloop/deps/kernel/kernel.wit,rust/components/wa-email/wit/deps/clocks.wit,rust/components/wa-whatsapp/wit/deps/clocks.wit,rust/components/model-gateway/wit/deps/clocks.wit,rust/components/svc-drain/wit/deps/clocks.wit,rust/components/svc-queue-echo/wit/deps/clocks.wit,rust/components/telemetry-sink/wit/deps/clocks.wit,rust/components/model-gateway/wit/deps/cli.wit,rust/components/model-gateway/wit/deps/filesystem.wit,rust/components/model-gateway/wit/deps/random.wit,rust/components/model-gateway/wit/deps/sockets.wit,rust/components/wa-email/wit/deps/cli.wit,rust/components/wa-email/wit/deps/filesystem.wit,rust/components/wa-email/wit/deps/random.wit,rust/components/wa-email/wit/deps/sockets.wit,rust/components/wa-whatsapp/wit/deps/cli.wit,rust/components/wa-whatsapp/wit/deps/filesystem.wit,rust/components/wa-whatsapp/wit/deps/random.wit,rust/components/wa-whatsapp/wit/deps/sockets.wit,rust/components/telemetry-sink/wit/deps/telemetry.wit,rust/components/svc-queue-echo/wit/deps/bus.wit,rust/components/telemetry-sink/wit/deps/bus.wit,rust/components/wa-email/wit/deps/bus/bus.wit,rust/components/svc-drain/wit/deps/queue/queue.wit,rust/components/svc-queue-echo/wit/deps/queue/queue.wit,rust/components/wa-email/wit/deps/queue/queue.wit,rust/components/wa-whatsapp/wit/deps/queue/queue.wit = lua5.4 scripts/gen-wit-deps.lua --write
